summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia s/p allogeneic cord blood transplant, chronic graft-versus-host disease, BOOP, and steroid-induced diabetes, was admitted from clinic due to fever, malaise, nausea, and fatigue. He had transient fever up to 102°F and one episode of low-volume diarrhea. Initial evaluation showed no acute pulmonary process on chest X-ray, but labs revealed acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine. Blood and stool cultures were ultimately negative. He was started on ciprofloxacin for possible enteric infection and transitioned from famciclovir to acyclovir for antiviral prophylaxis. Voriconazole was held due to a potential QTc interaction. His symptoms resolved quickly, kidney function stabilized, and he was discharged home after two days on a short course of ciprofloxacin with close follow-up instructions.
